data.title: Capricorn Metals Reports Karlawinda Results and Mt Gibson Permit Progress
data.description:
An update from Capricorn Metals Ltd ( (AU:CMM) ) is now available.

Karlawinda produced a record 124,000 ounces in FY26 at an all-in sustaining cost of A$1,629 per ounce, while its processing expansion from 4 million to 6.5 million tonnes annually was commissioned in September. The company reported FY26 operating cash flow of $470 million, net profit after tax of $327 million and cash and bullion of $508 million at year-end, rising to $535 million by the end of September.

Group Ore Reserves increased 33% over the past year to 5.24 million ounces, including 1.57 million ounces at Karlawinda and 3.7 million ounces at Mt Gibson. At Mt Gibson, the Federal environmental permit was issued in June, while the State permitting process had passed public exposure and was in its final stages before a State EPA decision.

Drilling and studies over three years increased Mt Gibson’s Ore Reserve by 250% and added a maiden underground reserve of 365,000 ounces. September-quarter drilling at Orion South returned 21.8 metres at 9.5 grams, while 26,700 metres drilled at Lexington and Hornet extended two lodes below the reserve pit outline, including intersections of 6 metres at 57 grams and 29.5 metres at 6.7 grams.

Capricorn paid its first fully franked dividend of 5 cents per share in April and a further 5 cents per share final dividend in October. The company said it owns two of the 13 ASX-listed Australian producing gold projects with more than 1 million ounces of Ore Reserves.

data.title: Metro Performance Glass reports unaudited 1H27 results
data.description:
Metro Performance Glass Ltd ( (NZ:MPG) ) has shared an announcement.

Unaudited group revenue for the six months ended 30 September 2026 rose 6% to $115 million from $108 million, while profit before significant items, interest and tax increased to $4.9 million from $1.0 million. Net debt declined from $27 million at 31 March 2026 to $26 million at half-year end, despite geopolitical uncertainty and softness in the markets in which the company operates.

New Zealand revenue increased 7%, while EBITDA as a percentage of revenue rose from 10% to 13% compared with the previous six months; DIFOT averaged 96%, and average daily insulated glass unit volumes increased 5% from the corresponding period. In Australia, growth was delayed by current economic conditions, although service and quality levels continued and product innovation remained part of the company’s market offering.

data.title: Legacy Minerals Reports Mt Carrington Resource Growth and Study Results
data.description:
Legacy Minerals Holdings Ltd. ( (AU:LGM) ) has shared an update.

Legacy Minerals is a resources company focused on mineral exploration and project development in Australia, with gold and silver as its primary commodities of interest and additional projects involving copper, nickel, cobalt, scandium and platinum-group elements. At its flagship Mt Carrington project, the company reported discoveries at the Mascotte, Emu and Battery prospects and a mineral resource estimate of 47.9 million tonnes containing 1.6 million ounces of gold equivalent.

The Mt Carrington resource is 39% above the 2025 estimate and 150% above the resource when the company acquired the project in July 2023, while indicated resources increased 69% from 2025. Development work included an Expanded Scoping Study assessing precious-metal concentrate production, a change from historic gold-only cyanide leaching; the study included 56% of the smaller 2025 resource estimate.

Elsewhere, Legacy Minerals executed farm-in agreements covering Cobar and Harden, divested the Glenlogan project, agreed a proposed royalty arrangement and farm-in option for Thomson, and reported work at Fontenoy, NiCo Young and Rockley. The company reported approximately A$3.5 million in cash at September quarter-end and described equity-market conditions as difficult for junior explorers and miners.

data.description:

data.title: Kairos Pharma Approves Executive Equity Grants and Bylaw Amendments
data.description:
An announcement from Kairos Pharma, Ltd. ( (KAPA) ) is now available.

On November 19, 2026, Kairos Pharma’s Compensation Committee approved an aggregate of 816,335 restricted stock units for certain executive officers under its 2023 Equity Incentive Plan. John S. Yu received 400,000, Neil Bhomick 200,000, Ramachandran Murali 16,335 and Doug Samuelson 200,000; each unit represented the right to receive one common share upon vesting and vested immediately upon issuance.

The grants were made in recognition of the officers’ services and to further align their interests with shareholders. The Board also approved an amendment and restatement of the bylaws on November 19, 2026, reducing the quorum required for a stockholders’ meeting from a majority of votes entitled to be cast to one-third; the amended bylaws became effective immediately after Board approval.
